reviews.title: eHarmony: Poison to Mental Health
reviews.text:
While cleaning up apps for space, I saw reviews that resonated with me so I wanted to share my experience even though it’s after the fact.

I deleted my eHarmony subscription after 1 year in August 2025 and leaving it unused since June 2025. I had high hopes in eHarmony because of the commercials I remembered as a preteen/teenager in the mid to late 2000s. Another friend married his lover through Facebook Dating so I had now-unfounded hopes that eHarmony would be a legitimate way to find love. Dating apps have historically been my only way to meet women because of not knowing where to develop connections in my current city outside work and life’s demands. Meeting possible dates in person seems risky anyway. I also need to focus on my career that was delayed by the pandemic and involved a switch to in-person work in a new city. I am in Texas where I am a Christian but I have poor relationships with most churches, making me uninterested in them. When I specified my faith as Christian, eHarmony mainly pulled up the fundamentalist, evangelical types I try to stay away from (also hurt my mental health in the past). But I am prone to people-pleasing so I changed my profile to appeal to this crowd early on. The platform was convincing early in its history but it has not changed with the times to improve match quality, expand its pool (especially for lonely/isolated people), or weed out scammers. reviews.title: Terrible App, Even Worse Cancellation Process
reviews.text:
My experience with eHarmony has been disappointing, to say the least. The app itself is underwhelming, but the cancellation process is where the real frustration begins.

Why does canceling a subscription require jumping through hoops, sending formal emails, providing account information, and practically writing an essay just to stop a company from taking your money? It makes absolutely no sense.

Signing up and taking my money was quick and effortless, but suddenly, when I want to cancel, it’s a complicated administrative process. If companies had to go through the same ridiculous procedures to collect payments from customers, they’d change their policies overnight.

I canceled my subscription approximately two months ago, yet I’m still being charged. Now I’m expected to go through additional steps to cancel something I already requested to cancel.

Here’s a revolutionary idea: If customers can subscribe with a few clicks, they should be able to cancel with a few clicks. No letters, no unnecessary emails, no obstacles, and certainly no begging a company to stop charging them.

eHarmony needs to seriously reconsider its customer service practices and subscription cancellation policies. Making it easy to take someone’s money but unnecessarily difficult to stop taking it is a terrible business practice.

I would not recommend this app. Save yourself the money, time, and frustration. Finding a compatible partner shouldn’t be easier than canceling a dating subscription.

reviews.title: I WANT MY MONEY BACK!!
reviews.text:
I WANT MY MONEY BACK!!

I’m stuck paying $200+ for a 3-month subscription, and I ran out of people to view on DAY ONE!

ALL profile photos are blurred unless you pay, so you’re basically forced to subscribe just to see who you’re actually considering. Then, once you’ve paid, there were barely any profiles within a 7-year age range, which is already a larger age gap than I want, and within the 30+ miles I’m already searching.

Then the app says to “Expand your search.” Meaning I have to increase the age range even more or search even farther away. For what?! 

And the worst part? You’re locked into the 3-month subscription and can’t cancel after realizing on DAY ONE that there’s no one to match with. They keep charging you for a service you’ve already exhausted.

Don’t waste your money. You’re better off on Hinge, CMB, Bumble, heck even Tinder. I wish I had spent my money on one of those instead, but instead I’m $200+ out, and no closer to meeting someone. 

I used eHarmony 2–3 years ago and had a completely different experience and was hopeful this time around too. 

Hundreds of dollars for what? I ran out of people on the first day. They clearly don’t spend the money to market towards the demographics they should (for reference, I’m 28).

After trying out the disappearing Match Group apps, I thought Eharmony would be different from the others because of the psychological theories behind it. I was too naive. Everyone was forced to subscribe at least half an year with a sum of over £250. It basically encourages everyone to stay longer to find the perfect match. However, most nice men seemed to be over one hundred miles away. You got recommendations of “perfect” matches frequently but was often disappointed by the silence after you expressed interests. After viewing so many profiles for four months, I am literally bored. Yes, Eharmony’s psychometric approach and high price policy did select a small pool of men with impressive profiles. However, they seemed to be unreachable. If you are looking for a men whom you can go out with, stay away from this app. I have paid the tuition fee and learned a lesson here.

reviews.title: So Many Scammers (UPDATE)
reviews.text: (UPDATE) — ***eharmony’s response is laughable. It’s been a month since I joined and if I could take a snapshot of my matches, it’s 8 total and all are scammers. These don’t include the almost daily scam requests I receive. I haven’t had one legit match or communication. If you sign up (and pay) for this service, you are a target and eharmony does almost nothing to prevent that from happening. It’s a terrible terrible service!!!!!***       “I’ve been using eharmony for just a week. In that time, I’ve received maybe 5-6 potential matches, all but one of which have been scammers. Of the different apps I’ve used, this is by-far the worst that I have seen, save those that are “free.” I had hoped that eharmony charging a bit more would cut down on the scam artists and bots, but unfortunately, that is not the case. I live in a mid-sized city (about 500K population), and the pool of potential profiles for a 20 year age range (32-52) is less than 100. Of those 100, at least a third are fakes. The real joke is that I signed up for a year’s subscription, so I’m on the hook for another 11 months of getting nothing for my investment except people using AI-generated photos to try and lure me off the platform and onto WhatsApp or Signal. It’s hard to fathom that in 2026, this company has such poor screening tools. Other apps at least make an effort to cut down on the fake profiles.

reviews.title: Steer well clear SCAMMERS
reviews.text:
eHarmony is honestly one of the most overpriced dating apps I’ve ever used. They lure you in with “compatibility” nonsense, then lock basic features behind ridiculous subscription prices. Paying that much just to message people is bad enough, but not even being able to clearly see someone’s photos unless there’s some kind of match is absurd. What’s the point of browsing profiles if half the experience is blurred out or hidden?

The whole app feels designed to pressure people into paying more while giving less. Expensive subscriptions, limited features, and outdated design choices make it feel like a scam wrapped in a “serious dating” label. For the price they charge, you’d expect transparency and actual functionality — not restrictions everywhere you click.

Save your money. There are far better dating apps that don’t treat basic interaction like a premium luxury.

reviews.title: BEWARE OF THIS APP!!
reviews.text: This app is just another repulsive money grab. For me personally, it was a ghost town. The only reason I even took the chance to download this app was because it was highly rated as “outstanding” by Forbes. It’s not. READ VERY CAREFULLY before buying the premium subscription, because if you get buyers remorse & decide to delete your account it’s impossible. They extort you & make you pay the ENTIRE 3 month subscription, as refunds are only available in 12 states in the US. Within a 3 day window as well. Eharmony is no different than any of these other dating apps that lock even the most basic features & filters behind a paywall. AN EXPENSIVE ONE AT THAT. Apparently, if you don’t pay them, they can send you to collections which will affect your credit score. I implore you, please think very carefully before using this app. If you contact customer care, I advise you to take screen shots of the conversations & keep all emails exchanged, for your protection. I have had more success with other alternatives, even a free one on a major social media platform. This is definitely a 0 out of 10. BUYER BEWARE.

reviews.title: Not very useful
reviews.text: I have an issue in respect to the App functionality. The App will not let you view additional profiles beyond the current one, unless you 💗 or X on the profile your viewing. I severely dislike this feature. I personally do not X a profile unless there is a significant reason in the profile to do so. In many cases profiles may seem nice, but have some minor issue, such as being "separated" instead of divorced, or not having a photo. In either case I would never hit the like button, but neither would I hit the X as those are things that might change and if I were to X a profile I would never see those changes. Potentially loosing a good connection. I'm sure there are a host of other things beyond these two examples that could change and would change my opinion on hitting the like💗 button. This problem severely degrades the usefulness of the mobile platform, while the main desktop website doesn't have this problem. I sincerely hope eharmony will have their IT team correct this problem and make the app useful again.

reviews.title: Fake Accounts and Fake Reviews
reviews.text: E-Harmony epitomizes fraud and dishonesty. Nearly all five-star reviews are fabrications; I've read them all, and most are just one-line comments lacking specific reasons for satisfaction. Additionally, 90% of their members are fake profiles, which explains why sending over 100 messages often results in no response. To inflate activity and create the illusion of a large community, they lure users into purchasing their outrageously expensive one-year annual membership for $495. They ask you to pay via their desktop website to avoid Apple fees. Once paid, they continuously charge the $495 annually unless you actively cancel—through both the app and the desktop site separately. They refuse refunds, prorated charges, or options for three-month plans. I intend to pursue legal action against their deceptive practices—faking member activity and misleading users into year-long commitments, then requiring separate cancellations on each platform. Victims should file complaints in small claims court or report their tactics online and to the Better Business Bureau to expose their dishonesty. They will likely respond with the same generic reply sent to hundreds of others. Even their so-called human representatives simply use automated responses, as fake as their fake profiles.

reviews.title: Scammers
reviews.text:
Avoid eHarmony at all costs. Their recurring billing is a deceptive scam — they lock you into automatic charges with barely any transparency, and canceling is intentionally difficult. I was charged again without clear warning, and customer support was useless. Don’t give them your credit card.
Refused a refund despite having sent an email when opening my account clearly stating that they did not have permission to bill my card without my express permission. I had to contact my bank and disputed the charges and got a refund from the bank. 
Companies that try to enforce the recurring billing as the default option usually do so for a reason - because customers wouldn’t resubscribe if they were given the choice.
Save your time and money and use Bumble, Hinge or Tinder - a fraction of the cost and far more people using them. The choice of people on eHarmony is limited due to the price… don’t be fooled into thinking you’ll see a different type of person, it’s just the same people that are on other dating apps that have given in to their curiosity and unjustified hype for an overpriced, underperforming app.

reviews.title: Don’t buy any membership and keep your money safe
reviews.text:
I purchased a two-year subscription last month and chose to split the payment into four installments of $117 each. About 45 days later, my account was frozen, and I was warned that if I don’t update my credit card information, I would lose access—and still be charged over $400.

I never requested to unsubscribe, and I explained that even though the platform is inactive and only a few people use it, I still want to keep my plan. Customer service said they canceled the automatic renewal for 2027, but I am still required to pay the remaining three installments. I told them I am willing to pay, but I need a clear statement showing the total amount, how much I’ve already paid, how much I owe, and the remaining balance.

Unfortunately, eHarmony’s customer service has been very poor. All I get are warnings, not real solutions. The platform feels outdated and poorly managed. I will consider filing a complaint with the BBB. Honestly, it’s not worth it, and I doubt anyone can find meaningful connections on this platform.

reviews.title: A classic dark-pattern subscription scam - avoid!
reviews.text:
I downloaded eHarmony on a friend’s recommendation, hoping to try something different from the usual dating apps. Unfortunately, the experience was deeply disappointing.

The app itself feels outdated and unintuitive, attempting to replicate platforms like Bumble or Hinge but without the same functionality or user base. Despite living in a major UK city, there were very few active users available, which immediately raised concerns about value for money.

What concerned me most, however, was discovering, only after signing up, that eHarmony locks users into a 12-month subscription, something that was not made sufficiently clear during the purchase process. After reading numerous similar reviews, I learned that many users have had issues cancelling within the 14-day cooling-off period, which is a statutory right under UK consumer law.

When I contacted customer support to cancel, I was told that because I had completed the personality questionnaire and briefly browsed profiles (I did not message anyone), I would be required to pay a £65 “value compensation” fee. In my view, this charge was not clearly or prominently explained at the point of purchase, nor does it feel proportionate to the limited use of the service.

Overall, the combination of a sparse user base, poor app experience, and unclear subscription practices makes this service hard to recommend. I would strongly advise prospective users to read the terms carefully and consider alternative platforms before signing up.
